author: Tim
title: Why Everyone Is Rewatching This Netflix Crime Drama
text:
A show called Good Girls is being called the best thing on Netflix and fans are watching it over and over again. It stars Christina Hendricks, Retta, and Mae Whitman and somehow still feels underrated even with more than a billion minutes watched.
One fan said: “This show is amazing, I legit loved every second.” Others said the cast is perfect and warned not to trust anyone, and someone else just said: “Ooh, this one is a masterpiece for sure.”
The series was created by Jenna Bans, who also worked on The Family and Off The Map. It has an 86% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and critics liked it too.
One reviewer said: “The series’ pace is lively as the plot continually thickens. It also ponders the idea of what happens when people cross a line.” Another said it had complicated antiheroes and bold storytelling that you usually don’t see outside cable.
Someone else wrote: “Audiences should tune in sooner rather than later to watch this gem. Even with high expectations, they can still expect to be thoroughly entertained.”
In an interview, Bans explained how the show came to be. She said: “I owed NBC a pilot, and I wanted to write something escapist and fun and chock-full of wish fulfilment and something that made my mom feel better about her life. It was a love letter to my mother.”
The story follows three suburban moms who decide to rob a grocery store so they can get out of money trouble and feel some control again. Bans said pitching the show was surprisingly easy.
She said: “When we pitched the show to NBC, it was all female executives: I’ve never had an easier pitch. I think I got three sentences in before one screamed, ‘We have to do this.’ It was the easiest time I’ve ever had. They just really got it right away, and they were really excited to do the show.”
Even though fans loved it and critics liked it, the show was canceled after four seasons. According to Retta, who played Ruby Hill, they were close to getting a fifth season, but it fell apart because of one person.
She said on a talk show: “I think it was a little too close to when [the writers] would have to start [season five scripts] and figure out story, so… no. Trust me. Trust me, Kelly! I’m salty!”
